question: Were internationally connected factories more resilient during COVID?
rationale: Compare pre-COVID international groups using the same incumbent cohort and trajectory states as R4.
scope: Full exact Word row, interpreted through repository minimum checks and current owner full-plan ning/full-row acceptance gates. All analysis below is planned, not executed.

target_estimands.name: Primary requested target
target_estimands.formula: q_it = alpha_i + lambda_t + sum_{t != 2019} beta_t D_i,pre 1[year=t] + u_it; q^L_it = L_it/L_i,2019 - 1; q^Y_it = Y_it/Y_i,2019 - 1; q^S_it = verified_alive_it

symbols.i: a verified establishment, never a row-number or artificial linkage
symbols.V: value added deflated with a certified appropriate price index; any single-output-deflator approximation is named
symbols.Y: gross output deflated with its certified output-price index
symbols.E: scope-defined verified physical energy in GJ; incomplete observed subtotals are separately named
symbols.C: scope-defined verified CO2 in metric tonnes; not automatically all greenhouse gases
symbols.L: workers under an annually verified employment definition
symbols.X: predetermined measured covariates declared for the particular design
symbols.g: verified treatment-entry cohort in calendar years
symbols.S: a verified trade, ownership, industry, or survival state; unknown is retained as unknown
symbols.q: a named outcome with its explicit closure and missingness rule
symbols.q^L_it: employment change as a fraction of positive 2019 employment
symbols.q^Y_it: real output change as a fraction of positive 2019 output
symbols.q^S_it: one for independently verified alive, zero for independently verified closure, unknown for unresolved absence

target_estimands.interpretation: beta_t is the difference in change relative 2019 for factories classified before 2019. State probabilities use the full R4 cohort; survivor productivity is a separate conditional target.
target_estimands.limits: Pre existing trends, foreign demand and selected integration remain alternatives to causal resilience. Few pre years make trend tests weak. Closure and missing observation have different implications for output/employment denominators.

decisions.primary_family: Three named outcomes (employment normalized level change, real output normalized level change, verified survival probability) by three frozen margins = nine complete 2020–22 average contrasts. State tables are descriptive. Missing survival evidence blocks the survival coefficient without blocking source-supported employment comparisons.
decisions.exposure_rule: Known 2017 and 2018 statuses; any participation primary. Both-years and 2018-only sensitivity. Do not add an unregistered 2019-only exposure definition.
decisions.models: Primary plant/year fixed-effect differential change for normalized employment and output and verified survival indicator. Certified baseline industry/province-by-year sensitivity uses its own support gate. State probabilities are the R4 model with frozen exposure contrasts, not an interchangeable survival estimand.
decisions.weights: Unweighted observed eligible records primary. Entropy balancing sensitivity matches first moments of 2017 and 2018 log employment and log Y within each exposure using only pre-2019 values; infeasible balance is unavailable. No outcome-dependent trimming.
